sentences.text: So, why don't you just pick one and that'll be it.

alts.text: Just pick one and you're done.
Perhaps you could simply choose one, and then the matter would be settled.

sentences.note: **why don't you just** 는 "그냥 ~하면 되잖아" 하고 망설이는 사람을 부드럽게 떠밀 때 씁니다. **that'll be it** 는 "그걸로 끝", 더 고민할 것 없다는 말입니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 8 | Friends

sentences.ko: 우리 집에서 내가 저녁 해 줄까?
sentences.text: How about if I cook dinner at my place?

alts.text: Wanna come over? I'll cook.
Would you like me to prepare dinner for us at my home?

sentences.note: **How about if I** 는 "내가 ~하면 어때?" 하고 내 쪽에서 뭔가를 해 주겠다고 제안할 때 씁니다. 집은 house 보다 **at my place** 라고 하는 게 훨씬 자연스럽습니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.ko: 우리 스키 타러 가자고, 뭐랄까, 초대를 좀 받았거든.
sentences.text: We were um sort of invited to go skiing.

alts.text: We kinda got invited skiing.
We received something of an invitation to go skiing.

sentences.note: **sort of** 는 "뭐랄까, 좀" 하고 말을 흐릴 때 씁니다. 꺼내기 조금 민망하거나 딱 잘라 말하기 애매한 소식을 전할 때 잘 나옵니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 머릿속에 말 좀 걸러 주는 게 있으면 얼마나 좋을까.
sentences.text: If only there was something in your head to control the things you say.

alts.text: Ever heard of a filter?
It would be wonderful if you had some way of controlling what you say.

sentences.note: **If only there was** 는 "~가 있기만 하면 좋을 텐데" 라는 뜻인데, 여기서는 생각 없이 말하는 친구를 비꼬는 말로 쓰였습니다. 말실수한 친구에게 농담 섞어 한마디 할 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 8 | Friends

sentences.ko: 내일 큰 발표가 있어서 그거 준비하느라 계속 바빴어.
sentences.text: JUST BEEN WORKING on this big presentation for tomorrow.

alts.text: Been swamped with tomorrow's big presentation.
I have been working on an important presentation for tomorrow.

sentences.note: "요즘 뭐 해?" 하고 물으면 I've 를 빼고 **Just been working on** ~ 이라고 짧게 답합니다. 계속 그 일에 매달려 있었다는 느낌을 줍니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 이 방에 사람이 좀 너무 많은 것 같은데.
sentences.text: There's a few too many people in this room.

alts.text: Way too crowded in here.
I believe this room has become somewhat overcrowded.

sentences.note: **a few too many**는 '필요한 것보다 조금 많다'는 뜻이에요. 모임 자리에서 눈치 주거나 에둘러 불편함을 말할 때 딱 좋고, 술을 좀 과하게 마셨을 때 **a few too many**라고만 해도 통해요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.ko: 이렇게 건강하게 헤어져 본 건 처음이야.
sentences.text: I have never had such a healthy breakup.

alts.text: Easiest breakup I've ever had.
That was the healthiest breakup I have ever experienced.

sentences.note: **I have never had such a** ~ 는 '이렇게 ~한 건 처음이야'라는 감탄으로, 좋은 경험이든 황당한 경험이든 다 쓸 수 있어요. 서로 싸우지 않고 좋게 끝난 이별은 **healthy breakup**이라고 해요.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 저녁 하라고 시켜 놓고, 한 시간이나 늦게 와서는 딱 하나 부탁한 것까지 잊어버려?
sentences.text: You forced me to make dinner, then you're an hour late and you forget the one little thing that I asked you to do.

alts.text: So I cook because you made me, you show up an hour late, and you forget the one thing I asked for?
After insisting that I cook dinner, you arrived an hour late and forgot the one small thing I had asked you to do.

sentences.note: **the one little thing**은 '딱 그거 하나'라는 뜻으로, 부탁한 게 별것도 아니었는데 그것조차 안 했다고 서운함을 강조할 때 써요. **an hour late**처럼 늦은 시간을 앞에 붙이면 '한 시간이나 늦었다'는 느낌이 돼요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.text: I don't know who made you the boss.

alts.text: Since when are you the boss?
May I ask who put you in charge?

sentences.note: 친구나 가족이 이래라저래라 할 때 받아치는 말이에요. **who made you the boss**는 '누가 너한테 그럴 권한을 줬냐'는 뜻이고, 비슷하게 **put you in charge**도 자주 써요.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 그래서, 그 여자 진짜 다시 만날 거야?
sentences.text: So, are you actually going to see her again?

alts.text: You gonna see her again or what?
Do you really intend to see her again?

sentences.note: 소개팅이나 데이트 이야기를 듣고 결론을 물을 때 쓰는 말이에요. 여기서 **actually**는 '말만 그런 게 아니라 정말로'라는 느낌을 더해 줘서, 상대가 망설이는 것 같을 때 넣으면 자연스러워요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends
